Q: Check two T values for inequality/current INotifyPropertyChanged syntax sugar/best practices A:

Welcome back.

Just use EqualityComparer<T>.Default.Equals(field, value). A quick search in mvvmlight found it in a commit from 14 years ago, feel free to dig deeper into the history or other mvvm libraries, if you dare.

I know, I know, back in the day, using an MVVM library was not common. They were out there, but most people just copied that ViewModelBase from the interwebs because that's all they needed, me included. And then you'd go snippet hunting - like you are now - trying to find that slightly more elegant implementation of RaisePropertyChanged() or whatever other part of the pattern. No problem with that, because there's not much code to it and it might not be worthwhile discussing the introduction of a package dependency to do this properly with your colleagues who would notoriously raise the change event unconditionally in the setter anyway. Jeeeez.

You look around one day and realize the things you assumed were immutable constants of the universe have changed.

Then Roslyn happened.

The foundations of our reality are shifting beneath our feet.

The MVVM Toolkit, successor of mvvmlight was created.

  • Introduction to the MVVM Toolkit
  • https://github.com/CommunityToolkit/dotnet
  • https://github.com/CommunityToolkit/MVVM-Samples

We live in a house built on sand.

And it brought an end to the snippet hunting, because it brings along code generators and other features which now make it very worthwhile to use the package instead of just duplicating some of its code.

latest syntax sugar and best practices for it are:

using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.ComponentModel;

public partial class PersonViewModel : ObservableObject
{
    [ObservableProperty]
    public partial string Name { get; private set; }
}

Q: How to receive a string parameter potentially containing slashes as a single value with a Codeigniter controller A:

One way to collect zero or more URL segments is to declare the second controller parameter as variadic (...). This captures all remaining slash-delimited URL segments. This will collect all remaining slash-delimited strings to the end of the url.

In the following demo, the controller method's second parameter is $idParts which is defined as a variadic parameter. The $idParts variable will be an array of zero or more elements based on the number of slash-separated values provided after the $lang value in the URL. If no value is provided after the lang segment, then $idParts will be an empty array. implode() on an empty array will return a zero-length string.

Demo:

public function index(string $lang, string ...$idParts)
{
    var_export([
        'lang' => $lang,
        'id' => implode('/', $idParts)
    ]);
}
URL lang id
My_Controller/index/en en [empty string]
My_Controller/index/es/ es [empty string]
My_Controller/index/es/foo es foo
My_Controller/index/fr/something/else fr something/else
My_Controller/index/en/item/34/public en item/34/public
My_Controller/index/it/name/for/this/can/be/12345 it name/for/this/can/be/12345

To clarifying the type hinting on the variadic parameter, imagine wanting to collect zero or more ids which are always represented as integer values. You could define a controller method like this to make all id values as int-type:

public function processIds(int ...$ids)
{
    foreach ($ids as $id) {
        // $id is already cast as an int-type value
        $this->User_model->doThing($id);
    }
    echo 'Did thing for: ' . implode(', ', $ids);
}

More generally, if individual values may legitimately contain /, URL path segments are probably the wrong transport mechanism. Consider using query parameters or URL-encoding the value instead. If you can control string value delimiters, it would be advisable to avoid using slashes as a delimiter in string values being passed via url segments.

Q: Why is Claude hitting limits instantly? A:

It depends on the packet that you use.

See the session that Claude is doing (what it sends and what it receives behind the scene, so you can debug).

To debug and see your sessions, you can use tools such as Claude IDE: https://pen-code.com/projects/claude-ide. It lets you search, resume, fork, and manage multiple Claude Code sessions, so you can reuse warmed-up context instead of starting over and wasting tokens.

Q: Closing connections within a using block A:

I think it's reasonable to suppose that an object implementing IDisposable should clean up its own resources and not require the close. Now it might not close as quickly as you might want, so you would manually close them yourself, but then you wouldn't use the using syntax.
